answer: Edge-disjoint path quota. Agents accept actions only when the sender’s recent connection graph yields k edge-disjoint routes to k distinct aged anchors, sampled randomly. A sybil cluster shares upstream links, so merged routes count once, like ember paths joining. Each identity must then rent and maintain separate relay routes and connection slots; reusing one jetty collapses its quota. At dawn the sampling seed rotates. Attacker cost: k distinct paths per identity, with added bandwidth, latency, and endpoint churn.
